title: A chapter ends
paragraphs: Four years is a long time to believe in something. I thought I was building a life with someone. Now it has ended, and I am left with the feeling that so much of my time, care and effort went somewhere I can no longer reach.

I gave a lot to these years. Looking back, it is painful to feel that it may all have been for nothing. The hardest part is not only losing someone. It is realizing how quickly trust can break, and how easily another person can make you question the feelings you once gave without hesitation.
Love can be generous, but it can also be cruel. Sometimes it leaves you with more questions than memories, and with the strange regret of having been sincere.
I'm writing this from Bangkok, at the beginning of a different chapter. I don't know what comes next. For now, I am letting this be an ending.

title: I packed my things and left
paragraphs: Today I packed my things and left. No big speech, no perfect ending, no moment that suddenly made everything make sense. Just my things, a decision I had been carrying for a while, and the feeling that I could not stay there any longer.

Four years is a strange amount of time to walk away from. It is long enough to build routines around another person, to make plans without even thinking about it, to imagine that the person beside you will also be there in the years you have not lived yet. You collect ordinary memories without noticing. A meal, a street, a room, a trip, a conversation that seemed unimportant at the time. Later, all of it becomes part of what you are trying to leave behind.

We had good moments. I do not want to pretend otherwise. There was love, there was excitement, there were places we saw together and days I will probably remember for a long time. But there was also a lot of damage. We both made mistakes. I made mine, and some of them were serious. I hurt someone I loved, and I have to be honest about that instead of finding a convenient explanation for it. I cannot ask for understanding while refusing to look at my own actions.

At the same time, taking responsibility for my part does not mean I have to ignore what hurt me. Trust had been broken more than once. We kept trying to move past things, but moving past something is not the same as repairing it. Sometimes you say you have forgiven someone because you want the relationship to survive. Then another difficult moment arrives and you realise that the old wound never really closed.

We left for a trip in September. We spent time in Da Nang, then everything changed again and we ended up in Bangkok. I think some part of me hoped that changing places might help us change something between us too. A different city can make life feel new for a little while. It cannot do the work that two people have been avoiding.

The situation we are in now is difficult in ways I did not expect. There are debts, no real financial safety net, uncertainty about where to stay and what happens next. Even basic things have become stressful. I am not writing this to make my problems sound dramatic. This is simply where I am right now. I do not have a clever plan or a reassuring answer.

What hurt most was seeing how differently we seemed to respond when things became serious. I wanted us to sit down and face the mess together. I was not expecting anyone to rescue me or fix everything. I wanted honesty, a clear conversation and the feeling that we were still trying to find a way forward as two people who had chosen each other.

Instead, I found myself questioning whether we were still choosing the same thing at all. Thoughts of returning to people from the past, looking for another possible way out, made me realise how little trust I had left. I cannot know every thought behind someone else's actions, and I do not want to turn this entry into a list of accusations. I can only say what it did to me: it made the future I had imagined feel impossible.

Maybe this relationship had been ending for longer than I wanted to admit. Maybe we were both holding on because four years is difficult to let go of. But time spent together is not a reason to keep going at any cost. It does not turn pain into a healthy relationship. It does not guarantee that two people can build a safe life together.

Leaving does not make me innocent. It does not erase the things I did or the ways I need to change. I have to take those things with me and deal with them honestly. I do not want to repeat this relationship in another form. I do not want anger to become my personality, or hurt to become an excuse for hurting someone else.

For now, I need to take care of the most immediate things. Find somewhere to stay. Figure out the journey home. Deal with the debt one step at a time. Eat, sleep, and get through the next day without making everything worse. The future can wait until I have both feet on the ground.

I feel exhausted. I also feel strangely quiet. There is grief, and there is anger, but underneath it there is a small sense that I have finally stopped arguing with something I already knew. I cannot build a life by constantly waiting for the next crisis to show me whether I can trust the person beside me.

I once thought the next chapter would begin with both of us. It will not. I do not know what it will look like now, and I am not going to pretend that I am excited about starting over. I just know that I have to start somewhere.
Today, that somewhere was the door. I picked up my things and left.
